problemStatement.plain: Can the minimal polynomial theory be generalized from matrices to abstract K-algebras? If two elements of an algebra are related by an isomorphism, they should have the same minimal polynomial.

proven: minpoly K (φ x) = minpoly K x for any AlgEquiv φ (from Mathlib)
minpoly K (φ x) = minpoly K x for any injective AlgHom φ (from Mathlib)
Conjugation by invertible matrix defines an AlgEquiv on Mat(n,K)
Matrix similarity preserves minpoly (derived from abstract theory)
knownResults.goal: Complete formalization of minpoly as K-algebra invariant

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: Proved minimal polynomial is invariant under K-algebra isomorphisms and injective homomorphisms. Built conjugation AlgEquiv for matrices, derived similarity result as corollary. 0 sorries, 8 theorems.

insights: Mathlib already has minpoly.algEquiv_eq and minpoly.algHom_eq - the abstract result exists
